text: Theo migrates catalog-api, cart-api, and checkout-api onto AKS using the parallel path Lesson 2 scoped — deploy each service onto the cluster, verify it, then flip Ingress traffic over. Catalog-api goes first since it's read-only and lowest-risk; checkout-api goes last, since every completed sale depends on it.

Pods say Running, but that's not the real bar. Theo hits each service's actual endpoints through the Ingress and confirms response shapes match the old infrastructure exactly, since this migration isn't allowed to change any API contract. He also spot-checks that pods landed on more than one node, not just one machine.

Here's the honest limit of today's check: Theo confirms pods are healthy and spread across more than one node, but he doesn't specifically check which availability zone each pod landed in, or whether that holds up once the HPA scales checkout-api from 6 replicas to 30 under real load.

At today's normal, pre-sale traffic, six pods spread across nodes happen to cover more than one zone anyway — it looks exactly like the healthy picture you'd want. That's a different, easier question than whether it distributes correctly under sale-scale load, which Lesson 8 and the sale itself in Lesson 9 are the real test of.
